description: Three pre-publish (7.4) investigations on main @ 5fa792a (post-SB4-port), 2026-07-12, each fanned out as a read-only sub-agent then reviewer-spot-verified. No secret-bearing file (.pem/.p12/.jks/.env/CLAUDE.local.md) EVER committed (git log --diff-filter=A verified). Boot 4.0.7 / Framework 7.0.8 / Security 7.0.6 / Tomcat-embed 11.0.22 / snakeyaml 2.5 / logback 1.5.34 / Hibernate 7.2.19 / Jackson 2.21.4+3.1.4 all past their CVE lines (spot-verified via dependencyInsight). commons-io pin holds (2.19.0 by constraint). (3) ZERO-CONFIG FAIL-SAFETY: FAIL-CLOSED — a bare adopter (dep only, no props, no SecurityFilterChain) gets deny-by-default at every layer: refusing subject extractor (trust-forwarded-jwt defaults false), NoOp role/directory suppliers (empty), HttpOpaClient denies on every error, and the starter registers NO SecurityFilterChain (spot-verified — only @ConditionalOnClass probes) so Boot's default authenticated chain governs. Every kill-switch default is the secure state; none widens on absence. ADR-0022 root_read_tag_exemption absent=STRICT confirmed.

During 1.1.0 pre-publish smoke-test prep, 'ENABLE_SPA=1 ./deploy.sh build' rebuilt opa-abac-catalog:local (12s ago) but left opa-abac-usermgmt:local at 3 days old. Since the session's library changes (HttpOpaClient.isSafePath fix + ResourceResolutionSupport record + mechanical edits) live in shared modules the user-service also bundles, running the smoke test against the stale usermgmt image would have tested OLD code on the enrichment/role-resolution path — a false-green. Both example services bake the library via a Gradle bootJar inside their Dockerfile, so each image must be rebuilt independently.
resolution: Before an ENABLE_SPA/ENABLE_USER_SERVICE smoke test that must exercise CURRENT library code, force-rebuild BOTH images explicitly: 'ENABLE_SPA=1 ./deploy.sh build' (catalog) AND 'docker build -t opa-abac-usermgmt:local -f example-user-management-service/Dockerfile .' (usermgmt). deploy.sh 'build' runs only build_image() = the catalog image; 'up' does 'usermgmt_image_exists || build_usermgmt_image', so an existing (stale) usermgmt image is REUSED, not rebuilt. Verify freshness with 'docker images | grep opa-abac' (CreatedSince) before trusting the smoke test.

First Maven Central publish (dev.dmitriikonovalov:opa-abac-* 1.0.0 via vanniktech 0.37.0 + Central Portal) failed FOUR times with 'Invalid signature … Could not find a public key by the key fingerprint' even though the GPG public key was provably on keyserver.ubuntu.com AND keys.openpgp.org (verified via op=get and op=index by full fingerprint). Misleading: the error names the keyserver, but the key WAS there. Real root cause: vanniktech signAllPublications() defaults to an IN-MEMORY (Bouncy Castle) signatory (signingInMemoryKey), which produces v4 signatures carrying ONLY the 64-bit issuer key-id (subpacket 16) and OMITS the issuer-fingerprint subpacket (33). Central's validator resolves keys by FULL FINGERPRINT (needs subpkt 33), so the signature is unverifiable regardless of keyserver state. Diagnosis that nailed it: 'gpg --list-packets <artifact>.asc' on the in-memory-signed file shows only 'subpkt 16 (issuer key ID)'; a signature from the local gpg BINARY additionally shows 'hashed subpkt 33 (issuer fpr v4 <FPR>)'. Secondary gotchas hit along the way: (1) 'gpg --send-keys' fails 'keyserver send failed: Invalid argument' on GnuPG 2.5.x here — upload via HTTP instead: curl --data-urlencode keytext@pub.asc https://keyserver.ubuntu.com/pks/add (HTTP 200 = ok). (2) keys.openpgp.org needs a JSON upload (Content-Type: application/json, {"keytext":...}) THEN an email-verification click before it serves the UID by email (by-fingerprint works pre-verification). (3) keyserver.ubuntu.com op=index by fingerprint lags ~40s behind op=get after an HTTP submit.
resolution: Sign with the gpg BINARY, not the in-memory key. Since build.gradle.kts uses vanniktech signAllPublications() (in-memory by default) and we don't want a repo change just for release mechanics, force it at INVOCATION time with a Gradle init script: allprojects { plugins.withId("signing") { extensions.configure<SigningExtension>("signing") { useGpgCmd() } } } saved to /tmp/use-gpg-cmd.init.gradle.kts, then './gradlew publishAndReleaseToMavenCentral -I /tmp/use-gpg-cmd.init.gradle.kts --no-configuration-cache'. Supporting ~/.gradle/gradle.properties: signing.gnupg.keyName=<LONGID>, signing.gnupg.passphrase=<pass>, signing.gnupg.executable=/opt/homebrew/bin/gpg (ABSOLUTE path — Gradle looks for 'gpg2' by default and errors 'A problem occurred starting process command gpg'), plus 'echo allow-loopback-pinentry >> ~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf && gpgconf --reload gpg-agent' so gpg takes the passphrase non-interactively. VERIFY before publishing: 'gpg --list-packets ~/.m2/.../opa-abac-core-1.0.0.pom.asc | grep "issuer fpr"' must print subpkt 33. Result: attempt 5 → 'Deployment is being published to Maven Central', BUILD SUCCESSFUL, all 6 coordinates released. RELEASING.md updated with all of this (PR #85). NOTE: failed Central deployments release NOTHING (validation gate) and leave a droppable FAILED entry — safe to retry. Applied 2026-07-12/13 opa-abac 1.0.0 publish.

name: vanniktech publish on a per-module allow-list: apply the plugin, but DEFER JavaLibrary config via plugins.withId
description: Wiring com.vanniktech.maven.publish (0.37.0) onto SOME subprojects (a library allow-list, never a blanket subprojects{} — the fail-closed edge: that would publish example/demo apps to Central) hits an evaluation-order trap. A root-level configure(subprojects.filter{it.name in allowList}){ apply(plugin=...); mavenPublishing{ configure(JavaLibrary(...)) } } FAILS at configuration time with 'Calling configure(JavaLibrary(...)) requires the java-library plugin to be applied' — because the root build script evaluates BEFORE each module's own build script applies java-library. Fix: apply the vanniktech plugin eagerly, but wrap the mavenPublishing{} + JavaLibrary config (and the -Xdoclint:none Javadoc tweak) inside plugins.withId("java-library"){ ... }, which fires exactly once when java-library arrives on that module — order-safe, no afterEvaluate needed. API notes for 0.37.0: publishToMavenCentral() is ARGUMENT-LESS (Central Portal is the default host; the old SonatypeHost arg is gone); signAllPublications() wires signing INTO the publish task graph (a publishToMavenLocal dry-run shows signMavenPublication in the graph — so no-key = publish FAILS at signing, never emits an unsigned artifact = fail-closed); JavaLibrary(javadocJar = JavadocJar.Javadoc(), sourcesJar = true) — sourcesJar takes a BOOLEAN in this line, NOT the SourcesJar.Sources() form some docs show. Verify the allow-list with a per-module './gradlew :MOD:publishToMavenLocal --dry-run' existence probe (exit 0 = task exists), NOT 'tasks --group publishing | grep -c' under -q (the -q output format drops the grep target and gives false zeros). Get the latest plugin version from Central maven-metadata.xml (repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/vanniktech/gradle-maven-publish-plugin/maven-metadata.xml <release>), NOT the Gradle Plugin Portal HTML (mislabels an old release as latest). Applied in opa-abac Maven-Central slice T1.

Adding a java-platform BOM module to a monorepo whose ROOT build has 'subprojects { apply(plugin="java") }' fails at configuration: 'The java-platform plugin cannot be applied together with the java (or java-library) plugin. A project is either a platform or a library but cannot be both.' The blanket subprojects{} block applies java to EVERY subproject including the new platform, which is mutually exclusive with java-platform. Symptom surfaces as a plugin-application exception on the BOM module's build.gradle.kts line where java-platform is applied, NOT on the offending root block.
resolution: Rescope the shared java block from 'subprojects { apply("java"); toolchain; tests }' to 'configure(subprojects.filter { it.name !in bomModules }) { ... }' with 'val bomModules = setOf("opa-abac-bom")'. The platform module then applies ONLY java-platform (+ the publish plugin) in its own build. Give the platform its own 'configure(subprojects.filter { it.name in bomModules }) { repositories { mavenCentral() } }' so it can still resolve the vanniktech plugin marker (the platform needs a repo but none of the java/toolchain/test config). Verify with an init-script probe: gradle.projectsEvaluated { subprojects.forEach { println(it.plugins.hasPlugin("java")+"/"+it.plugins.hasPlugin("java-platform")) } } — want 5 libs java-only, BOM platform-only, examples java-only-no-publish. A './gradlew build' that still runs the integration tests (40 tasks, all up-to-date) proves the rescope is behavior-preserving for the jar modules. General lesson: a blanket subprojects{apply('java')} in the root build is a latent trap for ANY future non-java module (platform, or a docs/aggregation module) — the fix pattern is a named exclusion set. vanniktech: configure(JavaPlatform()) for the BOM (POM-only + .asc, no jar/sources/javadoc) vs configure(JavaLibrary(...)) for jar modules. Applied in opa-abac Maven-Central slice T3.
